text: [excited] Google put an AI supercomputer in space.
[mischievously] Its very first answer... was a poem.
[curious] October 2026. A rocket full of small satellites lifts off.
One carries four of Google's AI chips: a tiny data center, in orbit.
[dramatic] Before launch, they blasted a chip with a proton beam.
[impressed] It only started glitching at nearly three times the dose it would get in five years.
Three weeks of tests later, the chips wake up.
[curious] Engineers send one message: write a haiku about being a chip orbiting Earth.
[whispers] Then they wait for it to come back around... over Norway.
[softly] Blue marble below. Data streams in silent grace. Starlight feeds my core.
[deadpan] Unluckily, it can only run one chip at a time... for about twenty minutes.
[curious] Why bother? On Earth, solar power is like a phone that gets unplugged every night.
In the right orbit, the sun almost never sets.
[excited] Next, in 2027: two satellites, talking by laser.
[playful] And the space poet's next assignment?
